problem: Portfolio facts change over time, while visitors ask open-ended questions. The assistant needed a reliable way to publish reviewed updates and answer from retrieved material without exposing trusted credentials to the browser.
purpose: Assemble portfolio exports, reviewed resume material, and approved supplements into validated knowledge versions; activate a complete version safely; and serve retrieval-grounded answers through the portfolio chat.
keyFeatures: Versioned knowledge assembly from portfolio exports, reviewed resume content, and approved supplements.
Version validation and controlled activation preserve the last good knowledge version when a candidate fails.
Relevant source pushes and production deployment events trigger synchronization; scheduled reconciliation provides best-effort periodic freshness.
Gemini embeddings retrieve evidence; Gemini or DeepSeek can generate answers with eligible fallback using the same retrieved evidence.
Bounded follow-up history supports conversational questions while each request retrieves current evidence.
A trusted portfolio server identity and Upstash Redis provide shared network-based chat rate limiting.
role: Led the RAG End-to-End build and portfolio-assistant integration across retrieval and generation, ingestion tooling, security boundaries, and the local-to-Vercel deployment path.
technicalHighlights: Portfolio exports, reviewed resume material, and approved supplements are assembled into a versioned candidate and validated before activation.
A verified activation switches the active knowledge version only after readiness checks, preserving the last good version on candidate failure.
Relevant source pushes, production deployment events, and periodic scheduled reconciliation initiate synchronization; scheduled timing is best effort, not a freshness guarantee.
Gemini embeddings retrieve source chunks once for generation; eligible Gemini/DeepSeek fallback uses that same retrieved evidence.
Responses include retrieved source records for whole chunks actually supplied as context. They are not statement-level citations and do not guarantee hallucination-free answers.
A trusted portfolio backend sends server-held authentication and HMAC-derived client identity; Upstash Redis shares a 10-per-hour network-based limit across instances.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: The assistant needs to handle broad natural-language questions without treating general model output as a reliable account of someone's work.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Retrieves focused, approved chunks before generation, caps the context passed to the model, and returns matched source records so the calling interface can review the grounding.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: The public chat experience needs API access, while ingestion and trusted server calls cannot expose administrative or bypass secrets in browser code.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Requires a trusted portfolio server to attach the API secret and server-derived HMAC client identity; Upstash Redis enforces the shared network-based chat limit across instances.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Portfolio updates, resume changes, and supplemental facts need different review levels, and partial uploads must not replace usable knowledge.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Assembles a versioned candidate, validates it in a separate knowledge collection, then activates only after verification. Resume updates and designated conflicts retain a review gate; failed candidates leave the last good version active.

resultsImpact: Keeps the active assistant knowledge aligned with reviewed portfolio changes through versioned synchronization and verified activation.
Preserves the last good version when a new candidate fails validation or readiness checks.
Returns source records for retrieved chunks so answers can be inspected against the supplied evidence, without implying statement-level citations or a guarantee against hallucinations.
lessonsLearned: How to implement RAG to LLMs through Redis-based vector retrieval, with a fallback to generation using the same retrieved evidence.
CI/CD pipelines can assemble a versioned candidate from multiple sources, validate it, and activate it safely without replacing the last good version on failure.
A versioned candidate and explicit activation gate make content publication safer than direct in-place updates.
Resume edits need review even when other portfolio facts can synchronize automatically.
Provider fallback is safest when it reuses the same retrieved evidence and context.
Trusted identity and shared rate limits belong in the server path, never browser-held secrets.
